India's relationship with health is 
changing. The question is no longer simply what is wrong, it is what can be prevented, personalised and if possible predicted. At the frontier of this shift stands diagnostics, quietly redefining its own role from a supporting act to the central protagonist of modern healthcare.
For Dr. Lal PathLabs, FY 2025-26 was the year we stepped into that frontier.
We did not just run more tests. We asked harder questions, of our science, 
our systems and ourselves. We launched Sovaaka, because we believed that precision health screening deserved its own language. We hosted Medllumina, because the future of diagnostics is a conversation that must happen at a global level. We continued to strengthen our specialised and precision diagnostics portfolio during FY26 through the introduction of 13 first-in-India and advanced diagnostic solutions across oncology, neurology, immunology and molecular diagnostics. Key additions included Amyloid Typing Solutions, Anti-AT1R Antibody, Mutated Citrullinated Vimentin (MCV) Antibody, Alzheimer’s Disease Biomarker Panel and Lymphnode AI Metadetect, reflecting our continued focus on innovation-led, personalised healthcare.
Driven by Innovation. Defined by Precision.Creating the Future 
of Diagnostics

laboratories, through our algorithms, by our people, for every patient who trusts us with their health.

DR. LAL PATHLABS LIMITED AT A GLANCE
Transforming Diagnostics  
Across India - Shaping the  Future of Healthcare
For over 75 years, we have remained a trusted partner in India’s healthcare 
journey, building a legacy rooted in diagnostic excellence, clinical reliability and patient trust.
Founded in 1949 by Dr. Major S. K. 
Lal, we have evolved from a single pathology laboratory into one of India’s most recognised diagnostic networks, delivering quality healthcare access across urban and emerging markets alike. Over the decades, we have continuously strengthened our capabilities across pathology, preventive healthcare and specialised diagnostics, while remaining committed to the highest standards of accuracy and care.
Today, we stand at the forefront of 
technology-led diagnostics, with a growing focus on advanced testing, genomics, precision diagnostics and preventive healthcare. Strategic initiatives such as Sovaaka and Medllumina	reflect	our	evolving	role in shaping the future of healthcare through innovation, scientific	advancement	and	clinical collaboration.
As healthcare increasingly shifts 
towards preventive and personalised care, Dr. Lal PathLabs continues to strengthen its position as a trusted healthcare partner, guided by science, enabled by technology and driven by a singular purpose: improving lives through accurate and accessible diagnostics.

To be the undisputed market leader by providing accessible, affordable, timely and quality healthcare diagnostics, applying insights and cutting-edge technology to create value for all stakeholders.

JOURNEY
Milestones that Shaped 
Diagnostics in India
From pioneering diagnostic technologies in India to building one of the country’s most 
trusted	healthcare	networks,	our	journey	has	been	defined	by	innovation,	expansion	and a relentless commitment to advancing healthcare access.
Foundation
1949
 Dr. Major S. K. Lal founded the 
Company in New Delhi, laying the cornerstone of trusted diagnostics in India.
1978
 Introduced automated haematology analysers in India, marking	a	significant	advance	in	diagnostic automation.
1982
 Pioneered franchising in the Indian healthcare sector through the establishment of collection centres,  a model that continues to	define	the	Company's	reach today.
 Introduced biochemistry autoanalysers in the region, raising the standard for clinical biochemistry testing.
1986
 Developed one of India's earliest Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS), enabling digitised and streamlined laboratory operations.
1989
	 Among	the	first	private	
laboratories in India to initiate HIV/AIDS testing, demonstrating early commitment to public health imperatives.
 Introduced Vacutainers for safer and standardised blood collection, improving both patient safety and sample quality.Building Scale & Credibility
1995
 Incorporated as Dr. Lal PathLabs Private Limited, establishing the formal corporate structure for future growth.
2000
 Three clinical laboratories received NABL accreditation, establishing the Company as an early benchmark for quality in organised diagnostics.
2001
	 Became	one	of	the	first	
laboratories in India to operate remote labs through satellite connectivity, pioneering distributed diagnostic services.
 Received ISO 9001:2008 certification,	affirming	commitment	to internationally recognised quality management standards.
2002
 Received CAP (College of American Pathologists) accreditation, among the most rigorous international quality benchmarks in diagnostics.
2004
 Entered a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) with the Government of Tripura, extending quality diagnostic access to underserved geographies.
2005
	 Became	one	of	the	first	Indian 	
healthcare companies to receive private equity investment, signalling institutional	confidence	in	the	organised diagnostics model.Cementing Leadership
2010
 Established Asia's largest National Reference Laboratory in Delhi, creating a world-class hub for high-complexity and specialised testing.
2015
 Introduced Electron Microscopy capabilities in private diagnostics, strengthening the high-end testing portfolio.
 Successfully listed on the NSE and BSE through an Initial Public Offering,	marking	a	defining	milestone in the Company's corporate journey.
2017
 Introduced Next Generation Sequencing (NGS) capabilities, entering the era of genomic and molecular diagnostics.
 Commissioned the Kolkata Reference Laboratory, anchoring the Company's leadership in Eastern India.
 Expanded international presence with the launch of a laboratory in Nepal.
2018
 Extended international footprint with the launch of a laboratory in Bangladesh, reinforcing the Company's South Asian diagnostics presence.
2019
 Launched the Genevolve Centre of Excellence for genetic testing, establishing a dedicated platform for advanced genomic diagnostics.
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26

Expansion
2020
 Established one of India's 
leading private-sector COVID-19 RT-PCR testing networks, demonstrating the Company's capacity to rapidly mobilise at national scale during a public health emergency.

2022
 Commissioned the Bengaluru Reference Laboratory, deepening the Company's footprint in Southern India and completing the South ecosystem build-out.

platform to strengthen advanced genomics and precision diagnostics capabilities

 Expanded the SwasthFit preventive healthcare portfolio alongside specialised offerings in genomics, reproductive health and autoimmune care

2025

 Expanded its R&D collaborations across academia (7 Academia-Industry partnerships) and healthcare & innovation ecosystems (3 Alliance with Start-up Ecosystem).Way Forward
As we enter the next chapter of 
our journey, our strategic priorities are clear:
	 Building	deeper	scientific,	
academic and healthcare 
ecosystem collaborations
 Advancing precision diagnostics and preventive healthcare across all patient segments
 Strengthening AI-led, genomics and molecular diagnostics capabilities
 Expanding geographic reach and deepening access across Tier 3, Tier 4 and rural markets
 Deepening international presence
 Driving the future of personalised healthcare in India, with science, scale and purpose

EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN'S MESSAGE
Dear Shareholders,
We have always believed that quality diagnostics 
should never be a privilege reserved for a few. It must be available to every person, in every city, and every community, with the same standards of accuracy, reliability and care. This belief has guided our organisation for over seven decades and continues to guide us through FY 2025-26 as well.
This was a year of meaningful progress for Dr. Lal 
PathLabs, not only in terms of growth, but also in how we continue to evolve as an institution serving India’s changing healthcare needs. As I	reflect	on	the	year	gone	by,	I	believe	we	are	standing at an important moment in the future of healthcare and diagnostics in India.
The world we are operating in
The global environment continues to remain uncertain. The world economy grew by 3.4% in 2025, yet geopolitical tensions,	inflationary	pressures,	commodity	volatility	and	supply	chain	disruptions	continued	to	shape	the	broader	business	environment.	 These	developments	influence	everything	from	medical	equipment	and	reagent	costs	to	long-term	
healthcare investments.
India, however, continues to demonstrate remarkable resilience and momentum. Real GDP growth stood at 7.6% in FY26, 
rising from 7.1% in the previous year. Per capita income continues to improve and new trade partnerships with major global economies are strengthening India’s long-term economic position.
More importantly, healthcare is steadily becoming central to India’s development agenda. The ambition of Viksit Bharat 
cannot be realised without stronger healthcare infrastructure, deeper preventive care and wider access to reliable diagnostics. In many ways, diagnostics today sits at the intersection of all three.Building India’s Most Trusted 
Diagnostics Institution for over 76 years
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26
08

=== page 12 ===
Why diagnostics has never 
mattered more
India’s healthcare challenge is 
becoming increasingly complex.  
We are home to nearly 101 million people living with diabetes and additional 136 million people with  
pre-diabetes. Hypertension now affects 230 million i.e. almost one in three adults. Lifestyle diseases are rising sharply among younger populations, while cancer and other critical illnesses are often diagnosed later than they should be.
At the same time, a large part of 
India still lacks access to dependable diagnostic infrastructure. For millions of people, especially across smaller towns and rural regions, timely diagnosis	remains	difficult,	delayed	or inaccessible.
This is why diagnostics has become 
far more than a healthcare service. It is increasingly becoming the foundation of modern healthcare itself.
What is equally encouraging is the 
visible shift towards preventive healthcare. More individuals today are taking ownership of their long-term wellness through regular health screening and early intervention. Wellness-led diagnostics continues to gain relevance across urban as well as emerging markets, and I believe this shift is still in its early stages.
For us, these trends reinforce one clear 
reality, the need for trusted, accessible and high-quality diagnostics in India has never been greater.
A company that keeps evolving
The healthcare industry is entering a new era, one shaped by genomics, precision	medicine,	artificial	intelligence and predictive healthcare. Diagnostics will play an increasingly important role in helping clinicians make faster, sharper and more personalised decisions for patients.At Dr. Lal PathLabs, we are consciously preparing for this future.
Over the years, we have steadily 
strengthened our capabilities in advanced	diagnostics,	scientific	research and technology-led healthcare delivery. During FY26, we continued to build on these foundations through investments in specialised testing, digital technologies and emerging areas of healthcare innovation.
What matters most to me is not simply 
the introduction of new technologies, but what they ultimately achieve, reducing uncertainty for patients, improving	clinical	confidence	and	enabling earlier intervention where it matters most.
This	year	also	reflected	our	growing	
role	within	the	broader	scientific	and medical ecosystem. Through deeper engagement with clinicians, researchers and healthcare institutions, we continue contributing to the advancement of diagnostics beyond the boundaries of our laboratories.
At the same time, we remain deeply 
conscious that technology alone does not build trust. Trust is earned slowly, through consistency, accuracy, ethical conduct and compassionate patient care over many years. That trust remains the strongest foundation of our organisation.
Shaping the future of diagnostics 
in India
The	next	decade	will	redefine	
healthcare globally, and India will be at the centre of that transformation. The organisations that succeed in this environment will be those that can combine	scientific	excellence	with	accessibility, digital capability with human judgement and innovation with responsibility.
That is the organisation we are striving 
to build.As we move forward, our ambition is not only to grow larger as a diagnostics company, but to help shape a more accessible, and patient-centric healthcare ecosystem for India.
Our success will continue to be 
measured	not	only	by	financial	performance, but by the trust that patients, doctors and communities place in us every day, trust earned through one report, one diagnosis and one life at a time.
In gratitude
I extend my heartfelt gratitude to every member of the Dr. Lal PathLabs family, our doctors, scientists, technicians and frontline teams, whose dedication and commitment continue to strengthen this institution each day.
I also thank our shareholders, partners 
and stakeholders for their continued belief and support.
Warm regards,
(Hony) Brig Dr Arvind Lal, Padma ShriExecutive ChairmanDr. Lal PathLabs LimitedFOR 76 YEARS, THIS

MESSAGE FROM THE CEO
Dear Shareholders,
As I present to you the Annual Report for FY26, 
I do so with immense pride and optimism. This year marked another important step forward in our journey of building a future-ready diagnostics organisation, one that combines medical excellence, technology and patient-centricity to deliver trusted healthcare outcomes at scale.
At Dr. Lal PathLabs, we remain committed to 
enabling healthier lives through accessible, reliable and high-quality diagnostics, while continuously advancing the future of precision healthcare in India.
Evolving Role of Diagnostics 
India’s healthcare landscape continues to evolve rapidly, shaped by rising preventive health awareness, increasing incidence of chronic diseases, expanding healthcare access and growing digital adoption. In this changing environment, diagnostics is becoming increasingly central to early detection, disease management and long-term wellness.
Expanding access across India
We expanded our network through the addition of 14 laboratories and more than 1,100 collection centres. Our cluster-led expansion strategy continues to strengthen our leadership in core regions while deepening our presence across Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets.
Today, our integrated network of reference laboratories, hub labs, cluster labs, satellite labs, patient service centres and 
franchisee partnerships enables us to deliver dependable diagnostics with improved turnaround time and operational efficiency	across	the	country.Powering the Future of 
Intelligent Diagnostics
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26
10

=== page 14 ===
Alongside network expansion, 
we continued strengthening our capabilities in high-end and specialised diagnostics across oncology, genomics, reproductive health, autoimmune disorders and infectious diseases. These investments position us strongly to address the growing demand for precision diagnostics and advanced testing in India.
Putting patients at the centre
We continued enhancing patient experience through faster reporting standards, improved accessibility and seamless digital engagement. We also expanded the reach of SwasthFit into Tier 2 and smaller towns, helping strengthen preventive healthcare adoption across emerging markets.
FY26 also marked the launch of 
Sovaaka, our AI-powered precision health screening and preventive wellness platform. Sovaaka represents an important strategic step towards science-led disease prevention and personalised health management by integrating advanced diagnostics, AI-supported imaging and curated wellness programmes into a differentiated healthcare experience.
Driving the future through 
technology and AI
We upgraded our enterprise technology 
infrastructure to a next-generation AI-enabled environment while accelerating automation across laboratory operations and customer interfaces.
We are now deploying AI across 
multiple use cases in cancer diagnostics, autoimmunity, antibiotic sensitivity, hematology and other departments. During the year, we also became	the	first	laboratory	in	India	to integrate a deep learning-based AI module for detecting lymph node metastasis, including micrometastasis, significantly	improving	the	speed	and	precision of oncology reporting.We further strengthened our genomics and molecular diagnostics capabilities through investments in advanced sequencing technologies and specialised platforms, with Genevolve continuing to expand our role in personalised medicine and high-complexity testing.
Advancing scientific leadership
Medical excellence continues to remain the cornerstone of our organisation.
A key highlight of FY26 was the 
successful hosting of Medllumina, our first	international	medical	conference	focused on the future of diagnostics and precision medicine. The conference brought together leading clinicians, researchers and global thought leaders to deliberate on emerging areas such as oncogenomics, transplant immunology, infertility, autoimmune diseases and rare genetic disorders.
We also strengthened our research 
and development initiatives through collaborations with academic institutions, international technology companies and start-up ecosystems, alongside expanding our in-house research capabilities.
Responsible and sustainable 
growth
As a healthcare organisation serving 
millions of patients, we recognise our broader responsibility towards society, communities and the environment.
During the year, we continued our 
efforts	towards	energy	efficiency,	waste management, responsible infrastructure development and environmentally conscious operational practices across the network. We also remained focused on building a safe, inclusive and growth-oriented workplace while continuing investments in employee capability development and medical training.Prepared for the future
We are entering FY27 with strong operational momentum, an expanded network, strengthened digital infrastructure and a future-ready portfolio of advanced diagnostic capabilities. Our focus going forward will remain centred on expanding access, strengthening preventive healthcare offerings, advancing specialised diagnostics and leveraging technology to create superior patient experiences.
We are helping shape a more precise 
and technology-enabled future for healthcare diagnostics in India.
Before I conclude, I would like to 
express my heartfelt gratitude to our patients, doctors, employees, franchisees, channel partners, shareholders and all stakeholders for their continued support. The dedication of our teams across the country continue to inspire us every day.
Warm Regards,
Shankha BanerjeeChief	Executive	OfficerDr. Lal PathLabs LimitedWE ARE HELPING

MESSAGE FROM THE GROUP CFO & CEO – INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS
Dear Shareholders,
I am pleased to have the opportunity to share 
this letter with you and express my gratitude for the	trust	and	confidence	you	have	placed	in	our	business over another year.
FY26 was a year that tested the strength 
and resilience of our business model. While delivering growth remains important, the quality of that growth matters equally — growth that is sustainable, supported by strong cash generation, operational excellence and the ability to create long-term value. On these dimensions, FY26 was a year of meaningful progress.
Delivering Consistent Growth
We	closed	FY26	with	revenue	from	operations	of	₹27,629	million,	representing	a	growth	of	12.2%	over	the	previous	year.	This performance was supported by healthy sample volumes, an expanding test portfolio and sustained demand across our diagnostic offerings.
What is particularly encouraging is not merely the growth itself, but the consistency with which the business continues to 
deliver. In a healthcare environment characterised by evolving patient expectations, increasing competition and changing industry dynamics, we have continued to strengthen our market position while maintaining a balanced and responsible approach to growth.
At the heart of our progress has been the trust placed in us by millions of patients, doctors and healthcare partners. Our 
continued focus on accuracy, reliability and service excellence remains central to strengthening this trust.
Our focus remains on building a business that can scale sustainably, supported by operational excellence, prudent 
investments and a strong commitment to quality. FY26 once again demonstrated the resilience of this approach.Compounding Growth with 
Discipline and Purpose
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26

=== page 16 ===
Strengthening Profitability Through 
Financial Discipline
Reported EBITDA for FY26 stood at 
₹7,524	million.	During	the	year,	the	Company recognised a one-time charge	of	₹301	million	related	to	the	implementation of the new Labour Code. Excluding this exceptional item,	EBITDA	stood	at	₹7,825	million,	reflecting	a	growth	of	12.5%	over	FY25.
Importantly, EBITDA margins remained 
steady at 28.3%, despite continued investments across technology, specialised diagnostics, digital capabilities and network expansion.
Maintaining margins while continuing 
to invest in future capabilities demonstrates the scalability of our operating model and the strength of our execution. Our ability to balance growth investments	with	profitability	remains	a	key competitive advantage.
Reported	profit	after	tax	stood	at	  
₹5,098	million,	compared	with	₹4,922	in	
the previous year. However, the year-on-year comparison was impacted by two non-recurring items: the Labour Code-related charge recognised in FY26 and	a	one-time	tax	benefit	recognised	in FY25 following the liquidation of Suburban Diagnostics (India) Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary.
Adjusting for these items provides 
a clearer picture of the Company’s underlying earnings performance. On	a	normalised	basis,	profit	after	tax	increased	by	17.9%	to	₹5,323	million during the year. This growth reflects	the	strong	fundamentals	of	our business and our ability to convert revenue growth into sustainable 
earnings expansion.
A Balance Sheet Built for 
Resilience and Opportunity
One	of	the	defining	strengths	of	Dr.	Lal	
PathLabs continues to be its robust financial	position.	We	remain	debt-free	and continue to maintain a healthy cash position, providing the Company with both	resilience	and	strategic	flexibility.
This	financial	strength	allows	us	
to pursue growth opportunities with	confidence	while	maintaining	a	conservative	risk	profile.	It	enables us to invest in capability building, strengthen our technology infrastructure, expand our service offerings and evaluate strategic opportunities without compromising financial	discipline.
Strong liquidity is not simply a balance 
sheet metric; it is a strategic advantage. It allows us to remain agile in a rapidly evolving healthcare landscape and ensures that we are well positioned to respond to future opportunities while maintaining	 long-term	 financial	 stability.
Throughout FY26, our capital allocation decisions continued to be guided by a clear framework centred on sustainable value creation, disciplined investment and prudent risk management. Our philosophy remains focused on investing in capabilities that strengthen our competitive advantage, evaluating strategic opportunities with prudence, and returning surplus capital to shareholders where appropriate.
Creating Sustainable Shareholder 
Value
Our commitment to delivering value to 
shareholders remained a key priority during the year.
In recognition of the Company’s strong 
financial	position	and	confidence	in	its	future prospects, the Board approved a 1:1 bonus issue and declared a total dividend of 280% on the equity share capital for FY26.
These	actions	reflect	our	confidence	in	
the Company’s long-term prospects and our	philosophy	of	sharing	the	benefits	of growth with shareholders while preserving	adequate	financial	flexibility	to support future investments.
We believe that sustainable shareholder 
value creation is best achieved through a balanced approach that combines	profitable	growth,	strong	cash generation and disciplined capital allocation.
As we continue to strengthen the 
business, our objective remains clear: to create long-term value while maintaining	the	financial	prudence	that	has been a hallmark of the Company 
over the years.Looking Ahead with Confidence
As	we	enter	FY27,	our	financial	
priorities remain unchanged. We will continue to focus on driving sustainable growth, protecting profitability,	maintaining	balance	sheet strength and allocating capital responsibly.
India’s diagnostics sector continues 
to	benefit	from	favourable	long-term	structural drivers, including growing healthcare awareness, increasing adoption of preventive healthcare, rising demand for specialised diagnostics and greater emphasis on early disease detection.
We believe Dr. Lal PathLabs is well 
positioned	to	benefit	from	these	trends	through its trusted brand, extensive network, quality-focused approach and strong	financial	foundation.
Beyond India, we continue to explore 
opportunities to build our international presence in a calibrated manner, leveraging our diagnostic expertise, operating capabilities and commitment to quality. Our approach remains focused on sustainable growth and value creation rather than growth for its own sake.
The investments we continue to make 
today are intended to strengthen our competitive position, enhance future growth opportunities and support sustained value creation for all stakeholders.
I would like to thank our shareholders 
for their continued trust and confidence.	I	also	extend	my	sincere	appreciation to our employees, healthcare partners and all stakeholders whose commitment and support continue to contribute to our success.
We remain committed to building an 
organisation that combines growth with governance, innovation with responsibility, and ambition with financial	prudence	—	creating	enduring	value for all stakeholders.
Warm regards,
Ved Prakash Goel Group CFO & CEO – International BusinessDr. Lal PathLabs Limited

OPERATING ENVIRONMENT & STRATEGY
Creating the Future 
of Diagnostics
Indian Healthcare & Diagnostics Opportunity
India	continues	to	present	a	significant	long-term	opportunity	for	
organised healthcare and diagnostics providers, supported by favourable demographics, rising healthcare awareness and increasing focus on preventive care.
 •The Indian diagnostic market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 
approximately	8-10%	over	the	next	five	years	
 •Organised diagnostic chains currently account for only around  15-20%	of	the	overall	market,	highlighting	significant	opportunities	for consolidation and market share gains by quality-focused national players
 •Rising awareness of preventive healthcare is accelerating demand for wellness and preventive testing services, which have emerged as one of the leading segments within the diagnostics industry
 •The total number of tests conducted by leading organised diagnostic players increased from 214 million in FY21 to 401 million in FY25, reflecting	 strong	growth	in	healthcare	 utilisation	 and	diagnostic	 demand
 •The number of patients served by leading organised diagnostic players increased from 64 million in FY21 to 99 million in FY25, supported by increasing healthcare awareness and broader adoption of diagnostic services
 •Despite more than 60% of India's population residing in rural areas, urban markets account for over 70% of diagnostic revenues, indicating substantial untapped opportunities across Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets
 •Rising per capita income, increasing healthcare awareness, an ageing population, expanding healthcare infrastructure and growing health insurance penetration continue to support long-term demand for diagnostic services
 •Genomic testing is emerging as an important growth segment, driven by increasing adoption in disease diagnosis, oncology and personalised treatment planning
As healthcare delivery increasingly shifts towards preventive, 
personalised and evidence-based care, organised diagnostic providers with strong quality standards, technology capabilities and scalable networks	are	well-positioned	to	benefit	from	the	industry's	long-term	growth opportunities.
Source: CareEdge Report ( https://www.careratings.com/uploads/newsfiles/1763463740_

disease caused by abnormal protein deposits in vital organs, identifying the exact amyloid subtype is critical. With over 40 known types requiring fundamentally different treatment pathways, diagnostic precision can directly	influence	patient	outcomes.When the Right

Until recently, patients across India and South Asia often had 
to	send	samples	overseas	for	definitive	diagnosis,	delaying	critical treatment decisions.
In FY 2025-26, we introduced Amyloid Typing  by Laser 
Capture Microdissection and Mass Spectrometry, becoming 
the	first	diagnostic	chain	in	South	Asia	to	offer	this	advanced	testing capability.

Why It Matters
This test enables precise 
identification	of	amyloid	subtypes,	supporting targeted treatment decisions where conventional methods may prove inconclusive. By bringing this capability closer to home, we are expanding access to globally benchmarked diagnostic precision for patients across the region.
The Science Behind the 
Breakthrough
The process combines Laser 
Capture Microdissection with Mass Spectrometry-based Proteomics to isolate and identify amyloid proteins with high precision, enabling accurate and clinically actionable diagnosis.
40+  Amyloid Types
Each requiring a distinct treatment approach
First in 
South Asia
We	are	the	first	diagnostic	chain	in	
the region to offer this capability
Pan-India  
Access
Samples from across India can be processed through our National Reference Laboratory in DelhiOther 12 tests, which are introduced 
as First-in-India are:
(a)   Complement Tests - C1q, C5 Serum 
and Factor B Antigen Serum, 
(b)   Epstein Barr Virus (EBV) Tests - EA-D IgM and EA-D IgG, 
(c)   John Cunningham Virus (JCV) Tests - Qualitative and Quantitative IGG, EIA,
(d)   Other Tests - 21-Hydroxylase Autoantibody (21-OH AB) Serum, Anti AT1R (Angiotensin II Type I Receptor) Antibody, Nocardia DST BMD, CA 27.29; Breast Cancer Marker Serum and Genital Ulcer Disease Panel PCR.

Building a Greener  
Healthcare Network   
At Dr. Lal PathLabs, we recognise that the responsibility of delivering quality 
healthcare extends beyond the laboratory. It extends to the planet we all share. Our environmental strategy is built on four pillars, Energy, Emissions, Water and Waste, and is embedded into every layer of our operations, from our National Reference Laboratory in Delhi to our growing network of satellite labs and Patient Service Centres across India.
In FY 2025-26, we made measurable progress on each of these fronts. Our 
investments in renewable energy, smarter systems and responsible waste management	reflect	our	long-term	commitment	to	sustainable,	environmentally	conscious healthcare delivery.ENVIRONMENT

Conservation
Managing energy consumption 
efficiently	across	a	nationwide	network of over 300 laboratories and 7,700+ Patient Service Centres is both an operational and environmental imperative. In FY 2025-26, we have continued to deepen our investments in	energy-efficient	systems	and technologies.
Solar Capacity Expansion
During the year, we installed a 42 kWh  
Solar Plant at our Panchkula and Cochin laboratories, taking our total installed solar generation capacity to 3.22 MW across the network. In FY 2025-26, this solar 
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26

=== page 40 ===
infrastructure generated

Power Quality & Load 
Management
 Power Factor maintained at up 
to 0.99 at high-consumption locations,	significantly	reducing	reactive power loss and improving overall	electrical	efficiency.
 Automatic Phase Sequence Corrector Panels have been installed across all locations, protecting equipment from phase imbalance and reducing diesel generator consumption.
 Power Capacitor Banks continue to be deployed at key facilities to reduce energy loss and enhance operational	efficiency.Cooling & Lighting Efficiency
 All laboratories and PSC locations are equipped with LED lighting. All new labs commissioned during the year	have	been	exclusively	fitted	with LED systems, eliminating energy-intensive conventional lighting across the network.
 R32 refrigerant-operated Inverter AC systems have been installed across operations. R32 has a significantly	lower	Global	Warming	Potential than older refrigerants and also conserves the ozone layer.
 On-delay timers installed in electrical rooms across 71 laboratories to protect and extend the life of AC systems, reducing both energy consumption and maintenance requirements. De-scaling of Chillers is carried out on a semi-annual basis to maintain optimal thermal	efficiency	and	reduce	energy draw.
 Inverter-based AC systems have progressively replaced conventional units across facilities, improving energy efficiency	and	reducing	peak	power consumption.
	 LED	retrofitting	continues	across	
the network, delivering reduced energy usage and longer service life across all facility types.
Emissions  
Reduction
Our emissions reduction strategy operates across three dimensions: switching to renewable energy sources, upgrading fossil-fuel dependent backup equipment, and improving	the	efficiency	of	power	and cooling systems to reduce overall consumption.
 17 new CPCB IV-compliant DG sets commissioned across pan- India labs, replacing older, higher emission models with equipment that meets the most current regulatory emission benchmarks	significantly	reducing	particulate matter and harmful gas emissions compared to earlier generation equipment.
 Descaling of DG Set radiators continues to be undertaken periodically to improve combustion quality and reduce smoke emissions.

=== page 41 ===
Water  
Conservation
Water is a critical resource in 
laboratory operations, used in reagent preparation, equipment cooling, sanitation and facility maintenance. We are committed to reducing consumption and maximising reuse across our network through a combination of technological solutions and operational best practices.
RO Wastewater Recycling
Reverse Osmosis (RO) systems are essential to laboratory-grade water	purification,	but	traditionally	produce	significant	reject	water	as	a by-product. In FY 2025-26, our RO wastewater recycling programme successfully recovered and reused approximately 9,125.3 KL of water that would otherwise have been discharged, channeling it instead towards non-potable applications such as washroom use and horticulture across our facilities.Digital Water Metering
Smart digital water meters continue to be installed across locations to enable more accurate, real-time monitoring of consumption patterns. This data-driven approach helps facility managers	identify	inefficiencies,	track	usage against targets, and optimise water consumption at each site.Water Recycling Infrastructure
The implementation of RO wastewater reuse systems has been progressively scaled across our network. These systems make the best use of available water resources while significantly	reducing	our	freshwater	demand and the environmental impact of discharge.
Waste  
Management
Laboratory operations generate both biomedical and general waste, each of which requires careful handling, treatment and disposal in compliance with regulatory requirements and environmental best practices. Our waste management framework is designed to minimise environmental harm at every stage.
Effluent Treatment
Effluent	Treatment	Plants	(ETPs)	are	
operational in all satellite laboratories across our network. These plants ensure the proper treatment of liquid laboratory waste throughout the year,	preventing	untreated	effluents	from entering drainage systems and helping maintain the environmental integrity of our operating locations.Biomedical Waste - Autoclave 
Infrastructure
In accordance with Biomedical Waste 
(BMW) Management Guidelines, all locations have been equipped with Advanced Autoclave systems. These autoclaves automatically record temperature, pressure and treatment time in graphical logs, ensuring complete traceability and compliance for every sterilisation cycle. This eliminates manual recording error and provides an auditable chain of evidence for regulatory purposes.
General Waste Practices
 Strict guidelines govern the segregation, treatment and disposal of both hazardous and non-hazardous waste at all facilities.
 Biodegradable bags are used for sample logistics across the network, reducing plastic waste at the point of patient interaction.
 Ongoing use of autoclaves for sterilising biomedical waste ensures safe treatment before disposal, consistent with BMW Guidelines.

=== page 56 ===
The Foundation envisions building 
a healthy nation by enabling access to high-quality, preventive healthcare services.
LPL Foundation contributes to 
healthcare and preventive healthcare services in the country by making an impact on the underprivileged section of society. To achieve this, LPL Foundation works with a focused approach	through	its	flagship	programs consisting of Vocational Training in Healthcare.
The purpose of the Foundation is to 
create	a	pool	of	certified	healthcare	workers to bridge the gap in the availability	of	qualified	healthcare	professionals and to provide sustainable livelihood for unemployed youth in rural, remote and semi-urban areas of the country.
Besides	the	flagship	programs,	the	
other focused thematic areas of the Foundation include Public Health — comprising health education to school children, awareness generation and preventive healthcare services, capacity building of the community, linking them to government health services, adolescent healthcare, nutrition support to tuberculosis patients, geriatric care, water and sanitation, and creating employment opportunities in rural and semi-urban areas.
Lal PathLabs Foundation is the CSR arm of Dr. Lal PathLabs Ltd. and its subsidiary companies.About Lal PathLabs Foundation

MANAGEMENT MESSAGES
Message from the Chairman
Our programs work on both 
sides of the healthcare equation — building the human resource supply that the system requires, while simultaneously equipping communities with the awareness and access needed	to	benefit	from	it. It is this consistency of intent, that transforms strong purpose into compounding impact.
(Hony) Brig Dr Arvind Lal, 
Padma Shri
Executive Chairman,  
Dr. Lal PathLabs Ltd.Science tells us that light travels in 
straight lines — but it is only when it passes through the right prism that a rainbow of colours is refracted. As Lal PathLabs Foundation stands today, we consciously align to the thought that genuine social responsibility goes far beyond meeting compliance obligations to the extension of consolidation, growing maturity and, a deliberate effort to scale impact.
We have sharpened our focus, 
refined	our	programs,	and	aligned	our work with a clear sense of what matters most: sustained, measurable improvement in the lives of the communities we serve.
Purposeful programs for 
compounding impact
Our	strong	purpose	finds	its	roots	in	
reducing the gap in the availability of quality healthcare for the most marginalised communities and linking regions	in	far-flung	areas	to	good	healthcare.	 Through	the	flagship		
program,  the LPL Academy for Laboratory Medicine – Phlebotomist Training Program, the Foundation addresses a structural gap in India’s allied health workforce by equipping young people from rural and semi-urban communities with employment-ready skills.
Public health programs — a 
continuum of interventions — move from early-stage health literacy and disease awareness in schools, through preventive screening for non-communicable diseases, to targeted support for high-burden conditions such as tuberculosis, cervical cancer, and chronic kidney disease.From Activity to Accountability
For much of Lal PathLabs Foundation’s early years, our CSR work was shaped by the imperative to act — to reach as many people as possible and address the most visible needs. In the recent past, our programs were evaluated	against	defined		outcomes,	and we used third-party assessments to inform how we adapt, scale, or redesign our interventions. This shift toward accountability ensures we continue our progress as a maturing foundation centred with the interest of our communities.
Scale and Depth of Impact
In FY 2025-26, Lal PathLabs 
Foundation’s	flagship	Phlebotomist	Training	Program	trained	and	certified	3,100 candidates across 20 training centres in cities spread across the length and breadth of the country. Since the program’s inception in 2018, over 13,000 phlebotomists have been trained	and	certified,	with	a	placement	rate consistently in the range of 80 to 82 percent.
These are not mere data points. 
Behind each placement, with every year-on-year percentage increase, there is a young person entering the formal workforce with a sustainable livelihood and contributing to healthcare delivery in their community.
On the Public Health front, Lal 
PathLabs Foundation reached over 1,00,000	direct	beneficiaries	across	42 locations, including villages, towns and union territory. Our programs spanned health education in schools, nutritional support for tuberculosis patients, NCD screening, 
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26

kidney patients, and cervical cancer awareness and screening.

Looking Ahead
The 20th LPL Academy for Laboratory

Purpose
Healthcare diagnostics is the front-
runner to any medical intervention for a patient needing medical care. Yet there is a shortage of skilled diagnostic professionals in rural and semi-urban areas. While the medical infrastructure initiated by the Government is available, skilled diagnostic professionals in and around the communities are inadequate. On the other hand, these regions lack sustainable employment opportunities for youth near their communities.
The LPL Academy for Laboratory 
Medicine-Phlebotomist Training Program addresses this gap by training local youth to become part of the diagnostic workforce. It also creates meaningful employment opportunities in regions where access to jobs is limited. In doing so, the program not only strengthens diagnostic capacity but also serves as a vital link between communities and basic healthcare services in underserved areas.
Program Goal
 •Bridge the gap in the need for skilled workers for delivering healthcare services in rural, remote and semi-urban areas.
 •Provide skilling and enable employability for rural youth to serve as the last-mile link in healthcare access in rural areas.Objective
Provide	dignified	
and sustainable livelihood to the unemployed youth through rigorous training as phlebotomists.Beneficiaries
Underprivileged, 
unemployed youth ages 18 years and above from rural, remote and semi-urban localities.Partners
 •B-ABLE Foundation
 •Lok Bharti Education Society
Dr. Lal PathLabs LimitedAnnual Report 2025-26

=== page 72 ===
Program Overview
The LPL Academy for Laboratory 
Medicine is Lal PathLabs Foundation’s flagship	initiative	to	train	youth	from	under-served	areas	as	certified	phlebotomists. These trained professionals act as last-mile connectors, linking patients in rural and semi-urban regions to diagnostic services and, in turn, to the broader healthcare system.
The program responds to two key 
challenges: the shortage of trained diagnostic personnel in expanding healthcare systems, and limited job opportunities for local youth. By developing relevant skills within communities, it creates a steady pipeline	of	qualified	professionals	while improving access to basic health facilities.The program that commenced with one centre in 2018, now operates 20 centres across 10 states and 2 Union Territories. It is recognised by the National Council for Vocational Education & Training (NCVET) and National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) and follows certification	standards	set	by	the	Health Sector Skill Council (HSSC).
The scope of the program now 
expands beyond technical knowledge. It integrates soft skills, workplace-readiness,	communication,	financial	literacy, gender sensitization, and entrepreneurial skills, ensuring well-rounded personal and professional growth. Trainees are also educated on infection control, pre-analytical errors, reporting, documentation, and medico-legal conduct, making them industry-ready professionals. This	has	helped	build	confidence	in	the phlebotomists as most of the candidates are freshers from high school with no prior work experience. There is support to the candidate from enrollment to post-placement follow-ups. 
In FY 2025-26, 2 new centres were 
launched - one centre in Ghaziabad, UP and the second centre in Kotdwar, Uttarakhand.
Lal PathLabs Foundation 
inaugurated the 20th LPL 
Academy for Laboratory Medicine – Phlebotomist Training Program at Kotdwar (Pauri Garhwal), Uttarakhand.
The inaugural ceremony was graced 
by Hon'ble Speaker of the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly, Ms. Ritu Khanduri Ji, and (Hony) Brig Dr Arvind Lal, Padma Shri, Executive Chairman, Dr. Lal PathLabs. This initiative aims to create sustainable livelihood opportunities for unemployed youth by providing specialised phlebotomy training, while also bridging the critical gap of skilled healthcare professionals across Pauri Garhwal and adjoining districts.
The Hon’ble Speaker commended 
this initiative and extended gratitude to Brig Dr Arvind Lal and Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited for bringing such a vital program to Kotdwar, Uttarakhand.

Impact Analysis
Compound Growth — 
Certifications
From 600+ in FY 2020-21 to 3,100+ 
in FY 2025-26 — a ~4.7x increase in annual	certifications	over	5	years,	a consistent 10 percentage point improvement over a 5-year period reflecting	expanded	centre	capacity,	improved intake and retention.
Placement Rate Trajectory
Placement rate improved steadily from 72% to 82%, indicating deepening relationships and stronger candidate	skilling/program	efficacy.Gender Inclusion
Female candidates grew from 48% to	62%	of	the	certified	cohort	—	a	deliberate shift that enhances healthcare access for women patients in rural areas and participation of women candidates in the formal workforce.
Geographic Expansion
Expanded from 8 states in FY 2020-21 to 10 states and 2 UTs by FY 2025-26, with overall 20 functional training centres, indicating a strong replicating model.Cumulative Leverage
13,000+ phlebotomists trained since inception — each serving an estimated 700+ patients per month. Healthcare access footprint for about 109.20 million patient interactions as of March 2026.
Investment Efficiency
As the program scaled, the patient touchpoints increased, cumulative income generation for candidates was at	₹1,600+	million	yearly.
Challenges & Our Response
 •Retaining female trainees in semi-urban areas due to family and mobility constraints.
 •Seasonal migration of youth and families in rural areas resulting in discontinuity.
 •Candidate dropout during the training period due to low maturity (18+ age) and ambiguous career aspirations or lack thereof.
 •Distraction and lack of focus among youngsters resulting in irregular attendance and not meeting	certification	criteria. •Parent & family engagement to reinforce long-term	benefits	of	vocational	certifications	and stable employment, especially for female candidates.
 •Trainee Counselling and Mentorship: Structured career counselling and motivational sessions were introduced to address personal challenges and strengthen career orientation.
 •Exposure visits to diagnostic centres and healthcare facilities helped candidates understand real workplace environments and career growth opportunities, improving retention and commitment.
 •Expanded the placement network to include government health centres, private clinics, and diagnostic chains; strengthened placement desk in each centre.
 •MIS tracking of attendance, assessment scores, and placement outcomes to identify at-risk candidates and provide timely interventions.
 •Alumni network, peer network among placed professionals and social media engagements.Challenges Response

Purpose
LPL Foundation’s Public Health pillar addresses 
six interconnected areas of community health need: grassroots preventive healthcare and health literacy; school health education and early NCD awareness; women’s cancer screening and early detection; renal disease management and chronic illness support; primary healthcare delivery strengthening and government health system integration; and nutritional support for tuberculosis treatment. Together, these areas form a continuum of care — from building awareness and early detection at the community level, to supporting treatment and recovery for those already living with disease. Each program is anchored in the principle that healthcare must reach people in underserved regions. The concerted effort in structuring these programs addresses both the gaps in service delivery and the barriers to receiving healthcare through awareness and access.

Monitoring & Evaluation
LPL Foundation has established strong MIS systems, SOPs and review 
mechanisms and systems and processes for project management, evaluation and continuous improvements. Program course corrections and continuous improvements are made based on internal program monitoring and intermittent external third-party evaluations.
Project Management
Daily WhatsApp updates ensure 
realtime communication and smooth project implementation nationwide. A monitoring checklist and SOPs guide the visit process.
Field Visits
Field visits — both announced and unannounced — follow a structured, checklist-driven process to assess project implementation through direct	engagement	with	beneficiaries	and stakeholders. Findings are documented in detailed reports and translated into actionable follow-up items with clear timelines.
Review Meetings &  
Technical Training
Monthly review meetings with implementation partners track progress and drive corrective actions. Capacity-building sessions each month strengthen technical expertise for	trainers	and	field	staff	in	the	LPL	Academy for Laboratory Medicine-Phlebotomist Training Program.Desk Review
Project data and reports are analysed regularly to assess performance and identify gaps. Findings directly inform continuous improvements by the implementation teams.
Data Management
The MIS portal provides end-to-end management of CSR project and	financial	data,	including	budgets, targets, timelines, and fund tracking. It also supports data management for the LPL Academy for Laboratory Medicine-Phlebotomist Training Program.
Media Communications
CSR projects and community impact are showcased through newsletters and social media across Facebook, LinkedIn, X, YouTube, Instagram, and the	official	website.	 These	channels	
engage	employees,	beneficiaries,	and	stakeholders through both traditional and digital communication.
Internal Communications
Regular emailers, newsletters, and structured updates to the Board ensure key stakeholders remain informed on project progress and outcomes. These communications maintain transparency and alignment across leadership and internal teams.

1. Introduction
  In terms of Section 178 of the Companies Act, 2013 
(“the Act”) and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015 (“the Listing Regulations) , this policy on nomination and remuneration of Directors, Key Managerial Personnel (KMP), Senior Management and other employees of the Company has been formulated by the Board of Directors on the recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration Committee of the Company. This policy shall act as a guideline for determining, inter-alia, qualiﬁcations, positive attributes and independence of a Director, matters relating to the remuneration, appointment, removal and evaluation of performance of the Directors, Key Managerial Personnel, Senior Management and other employees. other employees.
2. Policy Objective
 a.  To lay down criteria for identifying persons who are qualiﬁed to become Directors and who may be appointed in Key Managerial and Senior Management positions and to recommend to the Board their appointment and removal.
 b.  To lay down criteria to carry out evaluation of every Director’s /KMP/Senior Management Personnel and other employees performance.
 c.  To formulate criteria for determining qualiﬁcation, positive attributes and Independence of a Director.
 d.  To recommend to the Board a policy, relating to remuneration of directors, key managerial personnel and other employees. While recommending such policy the Nomination and Remuneration Committee shall ensure:
  i.  The level and composition of remuneration is reasonable and sufﬁcient to attract, retain and motivate Directors of the quality required to run the Company successfully.
  ii.  Relationship of remuneration to performance is clear and meets appropriate performance benchmarks.
  iii.  Remuneration of Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management involves a balance between ﬁxed and incentive pay reflecting short and long term performance objectives appropriate to the working of the Company and its goals.
 e. To formulate a Board Diversity Policy.
 f.  To recommend to the Board, all remuneration, in whatever form, payable to Senior Management.3. Definitions
 i.  “Board of Directors ” means the “Board of Directors” 
of Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited, as constituted from 
time to time.
 ii.  “Company” means Dr. Lal PathLabs Limited.
 iii.  “Independent Director” means a Director of the 
Company, not being a Managing or Whole- Time Director or a Nominee Director and who is neither a Promoter nor belongs to the Promoter Group of the Company and who satisﬁes the criteria of independence as prescribed under the provisions of the Companies Act 2013 (including the rules prescribed thereunder) and the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015.
 iv.  “Key Managerial Personnel” or KMP means 
key managerial personnel as deﬁned under the Companies Act, 2013 read with SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 & in relation to the Company means:-
  I.  Chief Executive Officer or the Managing Director or the Manager;

  IV. Chief Financial Ofﬁcer;
  V. Compliance Ofﬁcer and

5. Policy
 This policy is divided into three parts:
5.1  Appointment & Removal
 a.  Criteria for identifying persons who are qualified to be appointed as a Director / KMP/ Senior Management Personnel / Other Employees of the Company:
  i.  The Committee shall consider the ethical standards of integrity and probity, qualiﬁcation, expertise and experience of the person for appointment as Director, KMP or at Senior Management level and accordingly recommend to the Board his / her appointment.
  ii.  The Committee should ensure that the person so appointed as Director/ Independent Director/ KMP/ Senior Management Personnel shall not be disqualiﬁed under the Companies Act, 2013, rules made thereunder, Listing Regulations or any other applicable enactment for the time being in force.
  iii.  The Director/ Independent Director/ KMP/ Senior Management Personnel shall be appointed as per the procedure laid down under the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, rules made thereunder, Listing Regulations or any other applicable enactment for the time being in force.
  iv.  The other employees shall be appointed and removed as per the policy and procedure of the Company. b. Term / Tenure:
   The Term / Tenure of the Directors shall be governed 
as per provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and rules made thereunder and Listing Regulations as amended from time to time.
   The Term/Tenure of the KMP’s/ Senior Management Personnel and other employees shall be as per the companies prevailing policy.
 c. Removal:
   Due to reasons for any disqualiﬁcation mentioned in the Companies Act, 2013, rules made thereunder or under any other applicable Act, rules and regulations or any other reasonable ground, the Committee may recommend to the Board for removal of a Director, KMP or a Senior Management Personnel.
   The removal of other employees shall be as per the Company’s prevailing policy.
 d. Retirement:
   The director, KMP , senior management personnel & other employees shall retire as per the relevant provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 along with the rules made thereunder read with Listing Regulations and the prevailing policy of the Company, as may be applicable.
   The BOD, however, will have the discretion to retain, subject to regulatory approval, if applicable, the Director, KMP , Senior Management Personnel in the same position/ remuneration or otherwise even after attaining the retirement age, for the beneﬁt of the Company.
5.2 Remuneration
  The level and composition of remuneration to be paid to the Managing Director, Whole- Time Director(s), Non-Executive Director(s), KMP’s, Senior Management Personnel and other employees shall be reasonable and sufﬁcient to attract, retain and motivate directors, KMP’s, Senior Management and other employees of the quality required to run the company successfully. The relationship of remuneration to performance should be clear and meet appropriate performance benchmarks. The remuneration should also involve a balance between ﬁxed and incentive pay reflecting short and long-term performance objectives appropriate to the working of the company and its goals.

   The Whole Time Director(s)/ Managing Director

Global Economic Review 
In 2025, the global economy grew at a steady but moderate pace of around 3.4%1, supported by easing inflation, stable consumer 
demand and continued investment in technology and infrastructure. Growth has been pressured by rising geopolitical tensions, 
higher commodity prices and tighter financial conditions, with additional uncertainty from escalating conflicts. The situation has further intensified with restrictions on access to the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil shipping route, increasing risks to energy supply, trade flows and overall financial stability.

Indian Economic Review

Indian Diagnostic Industry
The Indian diagnostic industry is steadily evolving, supported by rising healthcare awareness, greater focus on preventive testing and improving access to services. The country is also witnessing a gradual demographic shift, with increasing life expectancy and a slowly ageing population. Despite this progress, the market remains highly fragmented, with over 3 lakh laboratories (estimated) across the country, most of which are standalone centres or Labs inside hospital and nursing homes. The estimates for the Indian diagnostic industry vary widely due to its fragmented nature; therefore, the analysis draws on multiple sources and internal assessments.
Organised diagnostic chains account for about 15–20%
5 of 
the market, indicating low consolidation, though their growing 
presence is helping improve standardisation, quality and operational efficiency. Government-led expansion of primary healthcare is expected to widen the testing base by bringing previously untested populations, especially in rural and semi-urban areas, into the formal diagnostic system.
Over the past five years, the leading organised players—
representing a sample set that accounts for nearly 10–12%
5 
of the overall industry—have strengthened performance, driven by higher patient volumes and a broader test mix. As per the CareEdge report, the total number of tests conducted across the sample set of leading organised players increased from 214
5 million in FY 2021 to 4015 million in FY 2025, reflecting 
strong growth in diagnostic volumes and increasing demand for healthcare and preventive testing services. Similarly, the number of patients served rose from 64 million in FY 2021 to 99
5 million in FY 2025. In India’s diagnostic market, urban 
areas account for more than 70%5 of revenues, even though 
over 60%5 of the population lives in rural areas, highlighting a 
clear urban–rural gap in access and adoption.

According to the IMARC Group, North and East India are

Outlook
The Indian diagnostic industry is expected to witness steady growth in FY2027, supported by rising awareness of preventive healthcare, increasing incidence of lifestyle diseases, an ageing population and India’s growing population base of over  
1.46 billion
6. Improving income levels, stronger payment 
capacity, expanding health insurance coverage and better access to healthcare services are expected to drive higher demand for quality diagnostic testing. While the industry remains fragmented, the sector is expected to sustain a medium-term growth rate of around 8–10%, driven primarily by increasing testing volumes and the gradual shift towards preventive and continuous healthcare management. Continued adoption of digital technologies, AI and integrated health records is expected to improve operational efficiency, diagnostic accuracy and patient experience, while rising investor interest and merger and acquisition activity are likely to support consolidation within the organised segment. The North and East region remains a key strength for Dr. Lal PathLabs, contributing approximately 77% of the business and offering significant long-term growth potential.
Growth drivers of the Indian diagnostic industry
Increasing Prevalence of Chronic and Lifestyle-Related Diseases: The rising incidence of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in India such as diabetes, cardiovascular disorders, cancer and respiratory conditions is driving growing demand for diagnostic services for early detection, monitoring and treatment. Factors like urbanisation, lifestyle changes and stress are contributing to chronic diseases, even amongst the younger populations. Diagnostic laboratories play a key role in screening, accurate diagnosis, treatment monitoring and preventive care. Additionally, India’s ageing population increases the need for regular diagnostic surveillance, creating 
opportunities for laboratories to expand specialised testing and chronic disease management solutions.
Expansion into Tier-2, Tier-3 and Rural Markets: A large share 
of India’s population resides in rural and semi-urban areas, while diagnostic revenues remain concentrated in major cities, reflecting a significant untapped opportunity. As healthcare awareness improves and access to medical services expands, demand for reliable diagnostic testing is steadily increasing in smaller towns. In response, organised diagnostic chains are strengthening their footprint across Tier-2, Tier-3 and Tier-4 markets through collection centres, partnerships and hub-and-spoke models.
Rising Focus on Preventive Healthcare: Growing awareness 
of preventive healthcare is becoming a key driver of growth for the diagnostic industry. More individuals are proactively opting for regular health check-ups, wellness packages and early screening tests to monitor and manage lifestyle-related conditions. Revenue from bundled packages catering to the wellness and preventive services has grown strongly over the past four years, with annual growth exceeding 25%
5 through 
FY 2025. Its contribution to total revenue has also increased significantly, rising from around 6–12%
5 in FY 2021 to nearly 
12–25%5 in FY 2025. Growing awareness of preventive 
healthcare, along with the launch of specialised packages, is expected to make this segment an important driver of future growth. This shift toward preventive and proactive healthcare, further supported by corporate wellness initiatives and digital health platforms, is driving increased demand for diagnostic services, particularly across urban and semi-urban markets.
Supportive Government Initiatives: Government-led healthcare 
initiatives and increased public spending are improving access to medical services and supporting growth in India's diagnostic and personal care sectors. Programmes aimed at strengthening healthcare infrastructure, expanding coverage and improving service delivery, along with digital health and teleconsultation initiatives, are making healthcare more accessible and efficient. A robust care ecosystem for geriatric (elderly care) and allied services will be developed, with National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) aligned training to upskill multiskilled caregivers in areas such as wellness, yoga and medical devices, targeting 1.5 lakh
7 caregivers in FY 2027. The Union 
Budget for FY 2027 further supports this momentum with higher allocations to healthcare, increased focus on medical education, research and digital health and continued emphasis on preventive care. These developments, coupled with rising health awareness, are expected to drive greater demand for diagnostic services and personal care products, supported by a growing focus on wellness, hygiene and overall well-being.

Opportunities
Digitalisation and Technology Adoption:  Technology adoption 
is reshaping the diagnostic industry by making services faster, more efficient and patient-friendly. The growing use of digital platforms, artificial intelligence and automation is streamlining laboratory operations and reducing turnaround times, while home sample collection services are improving accessibility and convenience for patients. Continued investments in advanced technologies and the development of specialised laboratories are expected to further accelerate growth in this segment and strengthen the overall diagnostic ecosystem.
Untapped Potential in Health Coverage: India’s health insurance 
ecosystem continued to expand in FY25, supported by wider coverage under government schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY and steady growth in private health insurance adoption. The inclusion of additional beneficiaries, particularly senior citizens, coupled with rising health awareness and increasing healthcare spending, is improving access to medical services across the country. For the diagnostics industry, expanding insurance coverage is expected to support higher utilisation of preventive healthcare, screening programmes and diagnostic testing, while the still-low penetration of health insurance presents a significant long-term growth opportunity.
Shift Toward Outpatient and Home-Based Diagnostics: The 
increasing global demand for convenient, affordable and faster healthcare services is driving growth in the outpatient care market. As a result, the market is projected to expand from USD 44

demand for accessible and efficient healthcare solutions. In India, the home diagnostic testing market is also expanding, valued at USD 223
9 million in 2025 and expected to reach USD 
3339 million by 2034, with a 5%9 CAGR. For the diagnostics 
industry, this trend is creating strong growth opportunities by increasing demand for outpatient and home-based testing, improving patient access and supporting the sector’s expansion into decentralised, patient-centric care models.

population aged 60 and above is expected to increase from  
10
10 crore in 2011 to 2310 crore by 2036, with their share in

The higher prevalence of age-related and chronic conditions, such as cardiovascular diseases and rheumatoid arthritis, increases the need for regular testing, disease monitoring and preventive health screenings. This demographic shift is creating a sustained growth opportunity for the diagnostics industry, driven by rising patient volumes, greater adoption of specialised tests and increased utilisation of advanced diagnostic technologies.
Growth in Advanced and Specialised Testing: Demand for

Reduced out-of-pocket expenditure is encouraging greater adoption of preventive healthcare and diagnostic testing. Industry Consolidation and Organised Sector Growth:  India’s

Backed by investments in digital capabilities, network expansion and enhanced testing infrastructure, these players are well-positioned to benefit from this ongoing shift.

International Expansion Opportunity for Indian Diagnostics:  
Indian diagnostic companies are well-positioned to expand 
internationally, leveraging their expertise in cost-efficient, high-volume testing and strong quality standards. Significant opportunities exist in underpenetrated markets across Asia, Africa and part of Middle East, where organised diagnostics infrastructure is still evolving. Their scalable operating models, competitive pricing and growing digital capabilities – such as telemedicine and remote reporting - enable efficient market entry and operations. Supported by rising global demand for preventive healthcare and early disease detection, as well as strategic partnerships in new geographies, Indian players have a strong opportunity to build a global presence and drive sustainable, long-term growth.
Threats
Intense Competition: The Indian diagnostics industry faces rising competitive intensity from organised laboratories, unorganised regional players, online platforms and digital health aggregators. Aggressive pricing strategies, discounted packages and bundled offerings from new entrants are exerting downward pressure on prices and reducing realisations in routine diagnostics. In addition, the entry of pharma companies, hospital chains and corporate healthcare players into the diagnostics space is further intensifying competition and increasing market fragmentation.
Regulatory Changes: The diagnostic industry operates under a 
more stringent regulatory environment, requiring laboratories to strengthen their quality systems, documentation and compliance processes. While evolving regulations supported better patient safety and service standards, they also increased compliance costs and operational responsibilities for diagnostic service providers.
Increasing point-of-care testing (POCT): The diagnostic 
industry is seeing the gradual entry of new players introducing Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) technology across clinics, pharmacies and home-care settings. However, adoption remains in its early stages, with limited traction so far, as central laboratories continue to dominate routine and specialised diagnostic testing and remain the preferred channel in the broader market.
Company Overview
Dr. Lal PathLabs (hereinafter referred to as “Dr. Lal PathLabs” or “The Company”) was founded in 1949 and has become a leading player in India’s diagnostics and healthcare sector. The Company, widely recognised for pioneering innovative diagnostic tests and cutting-edge technologies, continuously drives improvements in medical standards.
The Company operates a strong Pan-India network of 312 
clinical laboratories, including the National Reference Lab in Delhi and regional reference labs in Kolkata, Bangalore and Mumbai. Dr. Lal PathLabs supports its extensive network with more than 7,700 Patient Service Centres and ~ 14,000 Pick-
up Points, ensuring wide accessibility to diagnostic services across the country. Dr. Lal PathLabs has established dedicated specialty verticals, including Genevolve for genomics, L-CoRD (Dr. Lal PathLabs Centre of Excellence for Reproductive Diagnostics) for reproductive diagnostics and L-ACE (Dr. Lal PathLabs' Autoimmune Centre for Excellence) for autoimmune disorders, while further enhancing the Swasthfit platform to deliver comprehensive preventive healthcare solutions. With a comprehensive test menu of over 4,800 pathology and radiology tests and panels, the organisation continues to expand access to high-quality diagnostic services.
Following its IPO in 2015, Dr. Lal PathLabs introduced the 
SwasthFit bundled preventive health check programme as part of its efforts to expand into preventive healthcare. Over the years, the Company has continued to strengthen its diagnostic capabilities by adding advanced services, including Comprehensive Genomic Profiling and Myeloid Testing for Haematological Malignancies. More recently, in 2025, it further enhanced its specialised, precision-diagnostic portfolio by introducing various tests such as Amyloid Typing Solutions, Anti AT1R Antibody, Mutated Citrullinated Vimentin (MCV) Antibody, Alzheimer’s Disease Biomarker Panel, Lymphnode AI Metadetect etc reflecting its focus on advanced, personalised healthcare.
Dr. Lal PathLabs is actively integrating Artificial Intelligence-
based algorithms across multiple diagnostic areas, including Histopathology and Haematology, to enhance the efficiency, accuracy and reproducibility of diagnostic results. Dr. Lal PathLabs maintains high-quality standards through 53 National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL)-accredited labs and 2 College of American Pathologists (CAP)-accredited labs.
Operational Highlights
Key Achievements in FY 2026
The Company has approximately 141 million patient visits over the past five years, reflecting its strong nationwide presence and growing demand for its services. Dr. Lal PathLabs also strengthened its diagnostic portfolio with the introduction of more than 136 new tests, including over 13 “First in India” offerings, thereby enhancing its capabilities in advanced and complex testing. In addition, the Company’s technical team contributed to scientific advancement through more than 40 scientific papers in various national & international journals, including an award-winning study on the use of machine learning to rapidly diagnose acute leukaemia. A significant highlight during the year was the hosting of Medllumina 2026, a first-of-its-kind international medical conference by Dr. Lal PathLabs. The event brought together clinicians and global thought leaders to deliberate on the “New Era of Diagnostics”, with a specific focus on high-complexity domains.

10. Health and safety management system:
 a.  Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/ No). If 
yes, the coverage such system?
   The Company is committed to provide a safe working environment for our personnel, patients, clients, and visitors. It takes all possible steps to ensure the health, safety, and welfare of employees, and has developed a safety manual which is available to all lab personnel, and staff are encouraged to review it regularly.
   Staff working in the lab area are responsible for performing their jobs in a Safe prescribed manner, eliminating and/or reporting workplace hazards, accidents, incidents, and unsafe practices or conditions to ensure proper storage and disposal of all hazardous materials and wearing protective gear while handling samples.
   Additionally, annual health checkups are conducted for all staff involved in sample handling, and where necessary, staff are immunized with the appropriate vaccines.
   Further, we also undertake mock drills in relation to safety such as in cases of ﬁres and earthquakes i.e. in situations where immediate evacuation takes precedence. The Company’s operations are appropriately governed by evacuation signage boards which ensures that our employees are made aware of safety procedures, and we also ensure the availability of ﬁre equipment to ensure that we can effectively deal with ﬁre outbreaks.
 b.  What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis by the entity?
   The Company has carefully crafted comprehensive policies and guidelines to address various hazards and mitigate associated risks effectively. These policies provide a solid framework for identifying work-related hazards, following recommended guidelines, and conducting thorough risk assessments. Further, the Safety Manual outlines detailed procedures for risk assessment, ensuring employees have clear access to protocols and procedures. To ensure compliance with these policies, the Company has a Quality Department to monitor and evaluate adherence levels with the related policies.
   Further, our employees also play a great role in eliminating risk factors via reporting workplace hazards, reporting accidents, incidents, and unsafe practices or conditions to the applicable lab/facility supervisors, which in turn ensures that applicable hazards and risks identiﬁed are dealt with to avoid future recurrences
 c.  Whether you have processes for workers to report the work-related hazards and to remove themselves from such risks. (Yes/No)
   Yes, the Lab Safety Mannuals incorporates speciﬁc procedures that employees must adhere to in the event of safety incidents. These procedures delineate the appropriate steps and actions necessary to effectively address such situations. To ensure comprehensive incident documentation, the Company has developed a dedicated internal safety incident reporting tool.
   The report includes description of any event or accident, factors contributing to the event and information on ﬁrst aid or other health care facilities provided on the spot. This information is analysed with the purpose of effectively controlling repetitions and preventing future events. The records are checked periodically even in the absence of fresh entries.
   Supervisors or any lab staff are responsible for recording each safety incident on this platform, facilitating systematic data capture and analysis. Utilizing this reporting tool enables the Company to track safety incidents. Ultimately, this approach fosters a culture of continuous improvement in lab safety.
 d.  Do the employees/ worker of the entity have access to non-occupational medical and healthcare services? (Yes/No)
   Yes, the Company extends Mediclaim coverage to all employees except those falling under the ambit of the ESIC Act. Employees covered by ESIC receive all relevant medical beneﬁts under that scheme. Additionally, all employees are eligible for discounted diagnostic investigations.

5. Does the entity have a business continuity and disaster management plan? Give details in 100 words/ web link.
  The company has meticulously developed a comprehensive Business Continuity Plan (BCP) tailored speciﬁcally for its IT Services. The primary objective of this plan is to facilitate uninterrupted operations from an alternate location in the event of unforeseen circumstances or disruptions at the primary site. When the Disaster Recovery (DR) Plan is activated, the company’s IT systems seamlessly transition to the DR facility, strategically located in a different seismic zone. This geographical separation enhances the resilience and stability of the IT infrastructure. The BCP plan encompasses several key objectives:
 1. Timely Business Recovery:
   The plan aims to restore business operations within the agreed-upon timeframe outlined in the policy terms. This ensures minimal disruption and enables the company to swiftly resume operations.
 2.  Continuous IT System Functionality:
   The BCP plan guarantees that IT systems continue to function seamlessly from the alternate location until the primary site is fully restored. This uninterrupted availability of IT services is essential for maintaining business continuity and mitigating the impact on critical operations.
 3.  Crisis Response Guidelines:
   The plan includes detailed guidelines on how the company should respond during crisis situations. These guidelines assist in managing and mitigating potential risks and challenges associated with disruptiv e events
